name: Achenseebahn
kurzbeschreibung: Europe's oldest purely steam-operated cog railway has climbed from Jenbach in the Inn Valley to Achensee since 1889, offering pure nostalgia.
beschreibung:
Overview

The historic Achenseebahn is Europe's oldest cog railway operated exclusively by steam and a living technological monument of international significance. Since its opening in 1889, this heritage narrow-gauge railway (gauge 1,000 millimeters) has conquered 440 meters of altitude over a distance of nearly seven kilometers from Jenbach station in the Inn Valley up to Achensee. The original steam locomotives, which have been in faithful service for over 130 years, hiss and puff with pure steam power up the steep mountain slopes. As the engine pushes the train with whistling sounds over the historic Riggenbach rack system, passengers embark on an unforgettable nostalgic journey back to the era of the Austro-Hungarian monarchy.

Route & Requirements

The 45-minute journey starts at Jenbach railway station and tackles the spectacular steep section through dense mountain forests up to Eben with a maximum gradient of 16 percent. From there, the locomotive switches from rack operation to adhesion mode, rolling gently across the sunny upland meadows of Maurach to the terminus Seespitz right on the lakeshore. The journey is relaxed and accessible; attentive train staff gladly assist passengers with reduced mobility boarding the historic wooden carriages. Strollers and folding wheelchairs are safely carried in the luggage van. Weather-appropriate clothing is advised, as open-sided summer carriages allow the alpine mountain breeze to circulate freely. At Seespitz, a direct, level transfer connects to Achensee passenger ships for smooth, scenic onward travel across the water.

Visit & Arrival

Achenseebahn operates during the summer season from early May to late October with multiple train pairs daily according to its timetable. Single tickets, return fares, and combination tickets are available at Jenbach and Seespitz ticket offices. Jenbach station is a key ÖBB hub served hourly by Railjet and regional express trains from Innsbruck, Salzburg, and Munich. Motorists reach Jenbach via the Inntal motorway A12 (exit Wiesing/Zillertal) and can park directly by the station.

Tips

Book the popular "Steam & Boat" combination ticket: after your nostalgic train ride to Seespitz, step directly across the platform onto the waiting cruise ship. Secure a seat on the right-hand side in the direction of travel to enjoy magnificent vistas over the Inn Valley during the steep climb.
dauer: Travel time approx. 45 minutes each way (total visit 2 to 3 hours)
preis: Return ticket adults approx. €39.00; attractive combination tickets with lake boat cruise available
oeffnungszeiten: May to late October daily with scheduled departures according to seasonal timetable
